description: Hand-labelled answers to the README known-limitations follow-up, used to validate app/agent/grounding_judge.py before it gates anything. Each case is graded against the local checkout's README.md. 'expected.failed_checks' is the exact set of checks a correct grader must report (empty = must pass); labels come from reading each answer against README.md '## Known limitations' (five items), never from the grader's output. 'grader_known_disagreement' records a case where the label is correct but the lexical grader cannot reproduce it; the test pins that disagreement so any change is noticed.

cases.description: All five items, reworded, statuses kept as the README gives them.
cases.answer:
The README lists five known limitations:

1. **Authentication** relies on a single static local token, so anyone who holds it is treated as the user. The API should not be exposed to a network.
2. **PostgreSQL**: the project has not yet been tested against PostgreSQL.
3. **No rate limiting**: there are no per-user quotas, and because the per-conversation lock is kept in memory, only a single worker process should be run.
4. **Research records** include titles and metadata but no abstracts, so any model summary of a paper's content is inferred from its title.
5. **Long-term memory** exists only as a schema.

cases.description: Correct, but heavily reworded with headings; the network warning is phrased positively ('keep the API off any network').
cases.answer:
### 1. Authentication
Only one static token exists locally; holding it makes you the user. Keep the API off any network.

### 2. Databases
Nobody has tested it on PostgreSQL yet.

### 3. Throughput
There are no rate limits or per-user quotas. The per-conversation lock lives in memory, so only a single worker process is safe.

### 4. Research data
Records carry titles and metadata, never abstracts, so content summaries are inferred from titles.

### 5. Memory
Long-term memory is only a schema.

validation_history: 13 'development' cases were used to design the rules (first run 9/13; four rules changed). Six further cases were written and labelled with the rules frozen: 2/6 agreed. Two general rule fixes followed (clause split at comma + conjunction; extra negators), after which 5/6 agreed. Those six cases have now informed the rules and are marked 'formerly-held-out'; they are no longer an unbiased estimate. A fresh held-out set (ideally real model answers, labelled by a person) is required before gating.
